stem:
Ritu's father fits a convex mirror as the side-view mirror on his scooter. A similar convex mirror is also fixed at a sharp turn near her school gate.
Which statement best explains why convex mirrors are chosen for these uses?

options.text: Convex mirrors show objects at their actual size, so distances are judged correctly.
Convex mirrors form erect, smaller images and give a wider field of view, so more of the surroundings can be seen.
Convex mirrors form magnified images, so small objects behind can be seen clearly.
Convex mirrors converge sunlight, so the image formed is brighter than in a plane mirror.

teacher.key_rationale: A convex mirror always forms an erect, diminished image and, because it curves outward, covers a larger field of view than a plane mirror of the same size; this is why it is used as a side-view, road-safety and surveillance mirror. A is wrong because images are smaller than the object, C is wrong because images are diminished not magnified, and D is wrong because convex mirrors diverge light.
